verses.text: Yahweh appeared to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre as he sat at the entrance of his tent in the heat of the day.
He looked up and saw three men standing nearby. As soon as he saw them, he ran from the tent entrance to meet them and bowed low to the ground.
He said, "My lord, if you look on me with favor, please don't pass your servant by.
Let someone bring a little water so you can wash your feet. Then rest under the tree.
I'll bring some bread so you can regain your strength. After that, you can continue on your way, since you've come to your servant." They replied, "All right. Do what you've said."
Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah. "Quickly, take three seahs of fine flour, knead it, and bake some bread."
Then he ran to the herd, chose a tender, choice calf, and gave it to a servant, who quickly prepared it.
Abraham brought butter, milk, and the calf he had prepared, and set the meal before them. While they ate beneath the tree, he stood nearby.
They asked him, "Where is Sarah, your wife?" He answered, "She's there in the tent."
One of them said, "I'll come back to you around this time next year, and Sarah your wife will have a son." Sarah was listening at the tent entrance behind him.
Abraham and Sarah were already old, far along in years. Sarah was past the age when women have children.
Sarah laughed to herself. "After all these years, will I really experience this joy? And my husband is old too."
Yahweh said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh and say, 'Could I really have a child when I'm old?'
Is anything too hard for Yahweh? At the appointed time, about this same time next year, I'll return, and Sarah will have a son."
Sarah denied it. "I didn't laugh," she said, because she was afraid. But he replied, "Yes, you did laugh."
The men got up and looked toward Sodom. Abraham walked with them to see them off.
Yahweh said, "Should I keep from Abraham what I'm about to do?
Abraham is certainly going to become a great and powerful nation, and every nation on earth will find blessing through him.
I have chosen him so he will direct his children and everyone in his household after him to keep Yahweh's way by doing what is right and just. Then Yahweh will bring about what he promised Abraham."
Yahweh said, "The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and their sin is extremely serious.
I'll go down and see whether they've acted as badly as the outcry reaching me says. If not, I'll know."
The men turned away and headed toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before Yahweh.
Abraham came closer and asked, "Will you sweep away the righteous along with the wicked?
What if there are fifty righteous people in the city? Will you still wipe it out instead of sparing it for the sake of those fifty?
Surely you wouldn't do that—kill the righteous along with the wicked and treat both alike. Surely you wouldn't. Shouldn't the Judge of all the earth do what is right?"
Yahweh said, "If I find fifty righteous people in Sodom, I'll spare the whole place for their sake."
Abraham answered, "I've taken it on myself to speak to my Lord, even though I'm only dust and ashes.
What if five are missing from the fifty righteous? Will you destroy the whole city because five are gone?" He answered, "I won't destroy it if I find forty-five there."
Abraham spoke to him again: "What if only forty are there?" He answered, "For the sake of those forty, I won't do it."
Abraham said, "Please don't be angry with me, my Lord, but let me ask: What if thirty are there?" He answered, "I won't do it if I find thirty there."
Abraham said, "I've taken it on myself to speak to my Lord. What if there are twenty?" He answered, "I won't destroy it for the sake of those twenty."
Abraham said, "Please don't be angry with me, my Lord. Let me ask just one more time: What if ten are found there?" He answered, "I won't destroy it for the sake of those ten."
When Yahweh finished speaking with Abraham, he went on his way, and Abraham returned home.
